json.description:
Advice issued on 27 November 2026

A shark ADVICE has been issued following a technical fault affecting the latest iOS update of the SharkSmart WA app, released on 26 November 2026.

Situation: 

  • SharkSmart WA app iOS version 1.5.6 was released to the App Store on 26 November 2026.
  • A technical fault has been identified that is preventing some iOS users from updating to the latest version of the app.  
  • This appears to be an Apple-related issue and has been referred to Apple for further investigation.
  • iOS users are requested to not install version 1.5.6 of the SharkSmart WA app. Further advice will be provided when the matter is resolved. 
  • iOS users should not uninstall the existing SharkSmart WA app from their device, as previously installed versions remain fully operational. 
  • Android users are not affected by this issue. 
  • The SharkSmart WA website remains fully operational and is not affected. 

What to do:  

  • iOS users experiencing issues or new users wishing to download the SharkSmart WA app should stay informed of shark activity information by checking the SharkSmart WA website until the issue has been resolved. 

What authorities are doing: 

  • DPIRD will provide further updates as information becomes available from Apple. 

Extra information: 

  • Tagged shark detections from the Shark Monitoring Network and reported shark sightings have not been impacted by this fault and remain fully functional.
  • Shark activity information is still available by checking the SharkSmart website or following @SLSWA on X. 
  • If you see a shark, report it to Water Police on 9442 8600. All shark sighting information reported to Water Police is provided to land managers and relevant authorities.

Update on 13 October 2026 at 1:45 pm

The whale carcass, initially reported on the reef near Sandy Point Campground, has now washed up on reef south of Fourteen Mile Camp Beach, near Coral Bay.

A Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions (DBCA) Regulation 44 closure notice has been issued for the beaches between Stan’s Camp and Fourteen Mile, including The Ridge, and adjacent waters are temporarily closed for in-water activities. This closure does not apply to vessels. 

Additional caution is recommended by the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development (DPIRD) as the decomposing whale carcass and any residue may attract sharks to the Sandy Point Campground and Fourteen Mile Camp Beach areas.

Stay informed of shark activity information by checking the SharkSmart website, download the SharkSmart WA app or follow @SLSWA on X.

If you see a shark, report it to Water Police on 9442 8600.

json.description:
Advice issued on 27 November 2026

A shark ADVICE has been issued following a technical fault affecting the latest iOS update of the SharkSmart WA app, released on 26 November 2026.

Situation: 

  • SharkSmart WA app iOS version 1.5.6 was released to the App Store on 26 November 2026.
  • A technical fault has been identified that is preventing some iOS users from updating to the latest version of the app.  
  • This appears to be an Apple-related issue and has been referred to Apple for further investigation.
  • iOS users are requested to not install version 1.5.6 of the SharkSmart WA app. Further advice will be provided when the matter is resolved. 
  • iOS users should not uninstall the existing SharkSmart WA app from their device, as previously installed versions remain fully operational. 
  • Android users are not affected by this issue. 
  • The SharkSmart WA website remains fully operational and is not affected. 

What to do:  

  • iOS users experiencing issues or new users wishing to download the SharkSmart WA app should stay informed of shark activity information by checking the SharkSmart WA website until the issue has been resolved. 

What authorities are doing: 

  • DPIRD will provide further updates as information becomes available from Apple. 

Extra information: 

  • Tagged shark detections from the Shark Monitoring Network and reported shark sightings have not been impacted by this fault and remain fully functional.
  • Shark activity information is still available by checking the SharkSmart website or following @SLSWA on X. 
  • If you see a shark, report it to Water Police on 9442 8600. All shark sighting information reported to Water Police is provided to land managers and relevant authorities.

json.description:
Update on 13 October 2026 at 1:45 pm

The whale carcass, initially reported on the reef near Sandy Point Campground, has now washed up on reef south of Fourteen Mile Camp Beach, near Coral Bay.

A Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions (DBCA) Regulation 44 closure notice has been issued for the beaches between Stan’s Camp and Fourteen Mile, including The Ridge, and adjacent waters are temporarily closed for in-water activities. This closure does not apply to vessels. 

Additional caution is recommended by the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development (DPIRD) as the decomposing whale carcass and any residue may attract sharks to the Sandy Point Campground and Fourteen Mile Camp Beach areas.

Stay informed of shark activity information by checking the SharkSmart website, download the SharkSmart WA app or follow @SLSWA on X.

If you see a shark, report it to Water Police on 9442 8600.

Alert issued on 7 October 2026

Alert level:

A shark ADVICE has been issued due to a whale carcass being reported in waters off the Sandy Point Campground, north of Pelican Point near Coral Bay.

Situation:

  • The whale carcass was reported by Parks and Wildlife Service officers from the Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions at 12:00 pm.  
  • The whale carcass is located on the reef 1.5 km offshore, west of the Sandy Point Campground. 
  • It is possible the carcass will act as an attractant that could lead to sharks coming in close to shore along this stretch of coast.
  • Although sharks may be present along the Western Australian coast throughout the year, people should exercise additional caution. 

What to do:

  • Take additional caution in the Sandy Point Campground and Pelican Point area.
  • Adhere to any beach closures advised by Local Government Rangers, Parks and Wildlife Service officers or Surf Life Saving WA (SLSWA).
  • Stay informed by checking for shark activity on the SharkSmart website, SharkSmart WA app or follow @SLSWA on X.
  • If you see a shark, report it to Water Police on 9442 8600. All shark sighting information reported to Water Police is provided to land managers and relevant authorities and to the public on the SharkSmart website, SharkSmart WA app and @SLSWA on X.

What authorities are doing: 

Officers from the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development (DPIRD), along with staff from other agencies are monitoring the situation and providing advice to relevant authorities.

Extra information: 

Stay informed of shark activity information by checking the SharkSmart website – www.sharksmart.com.au/shark-activity, download the SharkSmart WA app or follow @SLSWA on X – x.com/SLSWA. Check www.sharksmart.com.au/news for updates to this alert and to view other warnings and media releases.

Advice issued on 27 November 2026

A shark ADVICE has been issued following a technical fault affecting the latest iOS update of the SharkSmart WA app, released on 26 November 2026.

Situation: 

  • SharkSmart WA app iOS version 1.5.6 was released to the App Store on 26 November 2026.
  • A technical fault has been identified that is preventing some iOS users from updating to the latest version of the app.  
  • This appears to be an Apple-related issue and has been referred to Apple for further investigation.
  • iOS users are requested to not install version 1.5.6 of the SharkSmart WA app. Further advice will be provided when the matter is resolved. 
  • iOS users should not uninstall the existing SharkSmart WA app from their device, as previously installed versions remain fully operational. 
  • Android users are not affected by this issue. 
  • The SharkSmart WA website remains fully operational and is not affected. 

What to do:  

  • iOS users experiencing issues or new users wishing to download the SharkSmart WA app should stay informed of shark activity information by checking the SharkSmart WA website until the issue has been resolved. 

What authorities are doing: 

  • DPIRD will provide further updates as information becomes available from Apple. 

Extra information: 

  • Tagged shark detections from the Shark Monitoring Network and reported shark sightings have not been impacted by this fault and remain fully functional.
  • Shark activity information is still available by checking the SharkSmart website or following @SLSWA on X. 
  • If you see a shark, report it to Water Police on 9442 8600. All shark sighting information reported to Water Police is provided to land managers and relevant authorities.

json.description:
Advice issued on 27 November 2026

A shark ADVICE has been issued following a technical fault affecting the latest iOS update of the SharkSmart WA app, released on 26 November 2026.

Situation: 

  • SharkSmart WA app iOS version 1.5.6 was released to the App Store on 26 November 2026.
  • A technical fault has been identified that is preventing some iOS users from updating to the latest version of the app.  
  • This appears to be an Apple-related issue and has been referred to Apple for further investigation.
  • iOS users are requested to not install version 1.5.6 of the SharkSmart WA app. Further advice will be provided when the matter is resolved. 
  • iOS users should not uninstall the existing SharkSmart WA app from their device, as previously installed versions remain fully operational. 
  • Android users are not affected by this issue. 
  • The SharkSmart WA website remains fully operational and is not affected. 

What to do:  

  • iOS users experiencing issues or new users wishing to download the SharkSmart WA app should stay informed of shark activity information by checking the SharkSmart WA website until the issue has been resolved. 

What authorities are doing: 

  • DPIRD will provide further updates as information becomes available from Apple. 

Extra information: 

  • Tagged shark detections from the Shark Monitoring Network and reported shark sightings have not been impacted by this fault and remain fully functional.
  • Shark activity information is still available by checking the SharkSmart website or following @SLSWA on X. 
  • If you see a shark, report it to Water Police on 9442 8600. All shark sighting information reported to Water Police is provided to land managers and relevant authorities.

Update on 13 October 2026 at 1:45 pm

The whale carcass, initially reported on the reef near Sandy Point Campground, has now washed up on reef south of Fourteen Mile Camp Beach, near Coral Bay.

A Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions (DBCA) Regulation 44 closure notice has been issued for the beaches between Stan’s Camp and Fourteen Mile, including The Ridge, and adjacent waters are temporarily closed for in-water activities. This closure does not apply to vessels. 

Additional caution is recommended by the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development (DPIRD) as the decomposing whale carcass and any residue may attract sharks to the Sandy Point Campground and Fourteen Mile Camp Beach areas.

Stay informed of shark activity information by checking the SharkSmart website, download the SharkSmart WA app or follow @SLSWA on X.

If you see a shark, report it to Water Police on 9442 8600.

Alert level:

A shark ADVICE has been issued following a technical fault affecting the latest iOS update of the SharkSmart WA app, released on 26 November 2026.

  • iOS users are requested to not install version 1.5.6 of the SharkSmart WA app. Further advice will be provided when the matter is resolved. 
  • iOS users should not uninstall the existing SharkSmart WA app from their device, as previously installed versions remain fully operational. 
  • Android users are not affected by this issue. 
  • The SharkSmart WA website remains fully operational and is not affected. 

What to do:  

  • iOS users experiencing issues or new users wishing to download the SharkSmart WA app should stay informed of shark activity information by checking the SharkSmart WA website until the issue has been resolved. 

What authorities are doing: 

  • DPIRD will provide further updates as information becomes available from Apple. 

Extra information: 

  • Tagged shark detections from the Shark Monitoring Network and reported shark sightings have not been impacted by this fault and remain fully functional.
  • Shark activity information is still available by checking the SharkSmart website or following @SLSWA on X.

  • The Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development (DPIRD) advise that the land-based shark warning system (tower) located at Surfers Point is experiencing a technical fault. 
  • The shark monitoring receiver adjacent to the tower remains operational and notifications of tagged shark detections will still be provided by the Shark Monitoring Network. 

What to do:

  • Take additional caution in the Prevelly area.
  • Adhere to any beach closures advised by Local Government Rangers, Parks and Wildlife Service officers or Surf Life Saving WA (SLSWA).
  • Stay informed by checking for shark activity on the SharkSmart website, SharkSmart WA app or follow @SLSWA on X.
  • If you see a shark, report it to Water Police on 9442 8600. All shark sighting information reported to Water Police is provided to land managers and relevant authorities and to the public on the SharkSmart website, SharkSmart WA app and @SLSWA on X. 

What authorities are doing: 

DPIRD is working with the Shire of Augusta Margaret River to restore the system to full operational status as soon as possible. 

Extra information: 

Stay informed of shark activity information by checking the SharkSmart website – www.sharksmart.com.au/shark-activity, download the SharkSmart WA app or follow @SLSWA on X – x.com/SLSWA. Check www.sharksmart.com.au/news for updates to this alert and to view other warnings and media releases.
